name: arrive_status
kind: service-axis measurement: result latency of an mbarrier arrive whose returned state is used; no workload-based fitting
question: How many cycles after it issues does a SYNCS.ARRIVE deliver the barrier state it returns (the instruction that reads the returned register can issue), for the arrive forms a kernel can write, compared with the same arrive whose result is discarded?
motivation: A user reports that the model under-charges SYNCS.ARRIVE when the returned state is consumed. In the trees SYNCS (every arrive form) has result and completion latency 1 cycle (structural.service_owner, never measured); the neighbouring class SYNCS.PHASECHK (try_wait returning its predicate) was measured at 37.9 cycles on both devices (barrier_release). None of the 1000 full-gpu suite cases contains an arrive with a destination register (all are `SYNCS.ARRIVE.. RZ, [..]`), so the corpus cannot show the cost; the probe is the only evidence.
probe: arrive_status.cu (mb.cuh helpers; one CTA on one SM; the barrier is initialised with a count large enough that no arrive of a window completes a phase unless the cell says so; bar.sync before every window). Chain cells: t0 = clock; U dependent arrives, each returning its state into a register that the next arrive's address computation reads (address = base + (state & 0), written so that ptxas keeps the dependence; the SASS must show the next arrive's address register derived from the previous destination); t1 = clock after an instruction that reads the last state; lane 0 records t1 - t0; U in {1, 2, 4, 8, 16}. Forms: arrive (mbarrier.arrive.shared::cta.b64 state, [addr]); arrive_cnt (.. state, [addr], count with count in a register); arrive_drop if the toolchain emits a distinct SASS form; expect_tx forms return no state and are not cells. Control discard: the same U arrives with the state written to a register nobody reads and the address independent (issue cost only). Phase cells: the last arrive of the chain completes the phase (count = U). Load cells: W in {1, 4} warps running the same chain on the same barrier (W = 4: contention on one barrier), and on four different barriers. 8 launches x 33 repetitions (repetition 0 discarded), runs a and b; H100 and B300.

controls.sass: window: exactly U SYNCS.ARRIVE of one form; chain cells: destination register not RZ and feeding the next address; discard cells: independent addresses; no other memory or sync instruction; actual mnemonics and operand forms recorded per cell.
controls.timing: runs a and b agree within max(2 cycles, 5 %) per cell; the per-arrive value is the least-squares slope over U and the fit residual is at most 5 % of the slope (else experimental).

derivation: L(form, cell) = slope of median(t1 - t0) over U for the chain cells = result latency of the arrive (plus the cost of the address add, taken from the alu leaf); I(form) = slope of the discard cells = issue cost.

predictions_before_data.engine_today: chain slope = 1 cycle result + the add (about 4-5 cycles per step); discard slope about 1-2.
predictions_before_data.guess: the returned state costs about what try_wait's predicate costs: 30-45 cycles per arrive on both devices, the same for arrive_cnt, larger when W = 4 warps arrive on one barrier.

outcomes_before_data.install: If L is at least 8 cycles above the engine's value and reproducible: the status-returning arrive gets its own operation class (classifier rule on both architectures: SYNCS.ARRIVE with a destination register other than RZ) with result_latency_cycles = L and the measured issue interval (instruction.service leaves, source arrive_status.<device>.r1); the discarding forms keep their class and values unless the discard cells also differ by more than 3 cycles from the installed leaf (then that is installed too). A dependence on W is reported and installed only if it follows a stated form.
outcomes_before_data.none: If L is within 8 cycles of the engine's chain value: nothing installed; the report is answered with the measurement.

prediction_check: H100 replay (tracer -> convert -> engine) of the arrive chain at U = 8 and U = 16 with the new leaf: within max(5 cycles, 15 %) per arrive; full-gpu 500 x 2 regression expected unchanged case by case (no suite case uses the form) - run for B300 and H100 only if the classifier change touches any existing case's class (checked by diffing the class tables of the converted suite captures of three cases per family).
not_allowed: No family / case / shape specific timing; no tuning to any workload's error; post-data changes of a criterion are labelled with their reason.

addenda.runs: $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/microbench/arrive_status/{h100-r3,b300-r3} (36 cells each, none dropped, SASS gate passed; r1 / r2 are failed rounds)
addenda.text: SASS of the forms (both devices): state returned and used: SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.A1T0 Rd, [..], RZ; with a count register: SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.ART0 Rd, [..], Rc; arrive_drop: SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.OPTOUT.A1T0 Rd, [..], RZ; state discarded: destination RZ. Cycles per arrive (slope over U = 1..16, residual <= 3 %; h100 / b300): chain arrive 40.24 / 40.00, arrive_drop 40.24 / 40.00, arrive_cnt 44.31 / 44.00; chain whose last arrive completes the phase 40.0 / 40.0; four warps on their own barriers 40.2 / 40.0, four warps on one barrier 35.1 / 35.0 (lower, not explained, not modelled); state discarded 3.83 / 6.00 (arrive, arrive_drop) and 5.51 / 8.00 (arrive_cnt). The chain step contains the probe's address arithmetic (LOP3 + IMAD on the returned register). The trees give every arrive form result latency 1 (class SYNCS, structural). Outcome 'install' for the state-returning forms: new classes for an arrive whose destination register is not RZ (one for A1T0 / OPTOUT, one for ART0), result latency = measured chain slope minus the arithmetic of the chain step, the latter taken from the H100 engine replay of the same chain on main (engine slope minus its present result latency of 1); B300 has no probe replay and uses the H100 arithmetic term (stated in the source entry; experimental). The discarded-state slopes (3.8 / 6.0 against an installed issue interval of 0) are replayed and reported; installing them would change every kernel that arrives and needs a full regression - not done in this step, recorded as open.

addenda.when: after the H100 replay on main (2026-11-15)
addenda.text: Replay of the arrive chain on main ($CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/fg-over20/arrive-replay-table.txt, journals under fg-over20/arrive-replay-sim): the engine issues consecutive arrives of the chain a steady 13 cycles apart (ARRIVE -> LOP3 2, LOP3 -> IMAD.IADD 5, IMAD.IADD -> ARRIVE 6), i.e. step = arrive result latency (1 today) + 12. Whole-window differences (252 - 94) / 8 = 19.75 include the repetition overhead and are not the step; the derivation uses the journal's arrive-to-arrive gap (stated after seeing the replay). Leaf values: result latency of the state-returning arrive = hardware step - 12: h100 28.24 (A1T0 / OPTOUT.A1T0) and 32.31 (ART0); b300 28.00 and 32.00, with the arithmetic term taken from the H100 replay because B300 has no probe replay. Check: the H100 replay with the new leaves must give an arrive-to-arrive gap within 15 % of 40.24 (chain) and 44.31 (count form).
